{!Contact.Name},
Thank you for your interest in the Ph.D. in Journalism and Mass Communication program at Arizona State University's Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication! I look forward to helping you learn more about our program.
About the Cronkite School Ph.D. Program The Cronkite School offers a student-centered, scholarly research-oriented Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in journalism and mass communication. The Cronkite School's doctoral program is interdisciplinary, and one of its hallmarks is the flexibility it gives students in choosing courses. Additionally, the program is focused on original research and faculty-student mentoring by nationally known scholars who also have professional experience in broadcasting, strategic media and public relations, new media and print. The program provides students with the opportunity for peer reviewed presentations/publications, in addition to the required scholarly dissertation.
For those who are more interested in learning the skills to practice journalism "in the field" (such as a reporter, writer, broadcaster, editor, etc.), the Cronkite School's master's program may be a better fit for you. Please feel free to ask me more information about that if you're interested.
Admission Students are admitted to start the program in the fall semester only. Applications should be submitted between September 1 and February 1 before the fall semester in which an applicant hopes to be admitted.
Our admission application requires submission of an online application, resume, personal statement, GRE scores, official undergraduate transcripts, three letters of recommendation, and a minimum score of 100 on the TOEFL exam (if an international student). A 3.0 undergraduate GPA is highly recommended, but not required. Students without master's degrees may be admitted but are required to complete additional course work.
If you have any further questions about the program or the admission requirements, please feel free to contact me.
Kindest regards,
